name: Spastic Paraplegia-Paget Disease of Bone Syndrome
aliases: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia with Paget Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spastic Paraplegia-Paget Disease of Bone Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Radiological evidence of Paget disease of bone (e.g., cortical thickening, bone enlargement)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with spastic paraplegia and Paget disease (e.g., VCP gene mutations)
Electromyography showing upper motor neuron signs without peripheral neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity plus radiological evidence of Paget disease of bone
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory. Family history supports diagnosis.

imaging: X-ray showing cortical thickening, bone enlargement, and trabecular coarsening consistent with Paget disease
MRI of spinal cord showing corticospinal tract degeneration
other: Electromyography consistent with upper motor neuron involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of Paget disease bone changes
Pure neurological involvement without skeletal deformities
No neurological symptoms such as spasticity
Localized bone involvement without upper motor neuron signs
Presence of both upper and lower motor neuron signs
Rapid progression and absence of Paget disease bone changes

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity with new neurological deficits
Pathological fractures or severe bone deformities
Onset of cranial nerve palsies or cognitive decline
references: Orphanet: Spastic paraplegia-Paget disease of bone syndrome, ORPHA:329475
Kimonis VE, et al. VCP disease associated with Paget disease of bone and hereditary spastic paraplegia. Neurology. 2000.
Harper PS. Practical Genetic Counselling. 8th Edition. 2018.
